fieldMarks: Small turtle, adults about 10-16 cm carapace length; smooth olive to brown carapace with no ornamentation.
Yellow chin (throat too in most areas), yellowish cheeks; four pairs of barbels on the throat.
Plastron black except where worn, with two well-developed transverse hinges; strongly webbed feet.
Male: slightly concave plastron, long thick spine-tipped tail; female: short stubby tail, flat plastron.
Emits a disagreeable musk odour when disturbed.
behavior: Diurnal in spring, crepuscular and nocturnal in summer; hibernates in winter and estivates in the hottest part of summer.
Seasonally aquatic then terrestrial: in the Illinois-Iowa-Missouri population turtles leave drying ponds in July-August and may be active under 100 days a year.
Often travels overland; adults wander about 190-220 m from water.
Omnivore: insects, mollusks, crustaceans, amphibian larvae, carrion and some vegetation.
habitat: Quiet or slow water with soft mud or sand bottom in grassland and open woodland, often temporary water; in arid regions in cattle tanks and ditches.
Seeks shelter underground on land or burrows in mud underwater.
range: South-central United States from Nebraska to southeastern Arizona, with an isolated population in Illinois-Iowa-Missouri; also northern Mexico.
